comments.body: Hi - thanks for the report. `jax_default_dtype_bits` is undocumented and has no test coverage: I would not recommend relying on it. We should probably mark the flag as deprecated and remove it in order to avoid this kind of confusion.
Got it, thanks. I appreciate you taking a look.

@jakevdp is the a particular reason the default dtype was changed from `jnp.{dtype}_` to `dtype` in https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/commit/f0309b49c92d2f3a69b26e432e77a9a1c124a8e0? I don't immediately see the reason for this. Would you accept a PR reverting `dtype` -> `jnp.{dtype}_` to fix this issue?

The 64 bit situation is still quite frustrating, I know there's been many attempts to fix this in the past but `default_dtype_bits` is fairly consistent except for `jax.random` calls. Would you accept contributions to get test coverage for `default_dtype_bits`?

The reason for this change was that `dtypes.float_` is `float64` even when `jax_enable_x64` is False, meaning that with that default there is no way to warn the user when they request an unavailable dtype. We would not accept a PR reverting that change, because it would break other code-paths.

We would not accept a change adding test coverage for `default_dtype_bits` because it's a mechanism that will not be feasible to support long-term.

Not sure I understand what you mean by warn the user when they request an unavailable dtype, this logic is implemented in jnp, no? In jnp you have the default as `dtype: DTypeLike | None = None` and then call `dtypes.check_user_dtype_supported` (which is a noop for None) before defaulting to `dtypes.float_` and finally canonicalizing the dtype.

I understand why you don't want to support this long term, but can we at least make it consistent with jnp? I have no issues contributing this myself.
Sure, setting the default to `None` would be an option, but reverting the commit you linked to would not.
I had a draft PR doing something like this in https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/pull/15177, but we were never able to land it because it led to downstream failures that were difficult to fix.
We're starting the process of removing `jax_default_dtype_bits` in #30962. I'm going to close this issue – thanks!

issue.body:
### Description

It looks like between v0.4.14 and v0.4.16 the `jax.random` functions stopped following `jax_default_dtype_bits`.

I'm not sure whether this is an intentional behavior change, but it looks like it might have been introduced in f0309b4 when the random functions switched from using `dtypes.float_` and `dtypes.int_` to plain `float` and `int` as defaults. It looks like the numpy array creation functions (like `jnp.zeros`) [still use](https://github.com/google/jax/blob/f0309b49c92d2f3a69b26e432e77a9a1c124a8e0/jax/_src/numpy/lax_numpy.py#L216-L226) `dtypes.float_`.

Thanks!

A couple sample sessions below:

I enable float64 and set the default dtype bits with environment variables:
```
$ JAX_ENABLE_X64=True JAX_DEFAULT_DTYPE_BITS=32 python
```

Running with `jax[cpu]==0.4.16`:
```
>>> import jax, jax.numpy as jnp
>>> jax.random.uniform(jax.random.PRNGKey(0)).dtype
dtype('float64')
>>> jnp.zeros(1).dtype
dtype('float32')
```

whereas with `jax[cpu]==0.4.14`:
```
>>> import jax, jax.numpy as jnp
>>> jax.random.uniform(jax.random.PRNGKey(0)).dtype
dtype('float32')
>>> jnp.zeros(1).dtype
dtype('float32')
```

### What jax/jaxlib version are you using?

jax v0.4.16, jaxlib v0.4.16

### Which accelerator(s) are you using?

CPU

### Additional system info

Python 3.11, Linux

### NVIDIA GPU info

_No response_
issue.title: `jax.random` functions don't follow `jax_default_dtype_bits`

issue.body:
This PR assures that the inferred dtype of `ops.array` and `ops.convert_to_tensor` remains consistent across different backends.

It is worth noting that overhead is introduced in `ops.convert_to_tensor` when the incoming dtype is `None`. Please let me know if it is not suitable.

A future warning:
`JAX_DEFAULT_DTYPE_BITS=32` is not working with `jnp.array` and it should be considered as not maintained in the future. https://github.com/google/jax/issues/17842
The unit tests of dtype might require some refactoring because they relies on `JAX_DEFAULT_DTYPE_BITS`. However, I don't have a clear idea about it at the moment.
I've added the extra logic for jax in the unit tests as a temporary fix.
issue.title: Apply `backend.result_type` to `array` and `convert_to_tensor`
